reviews.review: I love this game. 1st person shooters with larger maps are fine and all, but this game really does it for me. The community is mostly adults from what I can tell, but that hasn't stopped me from having fun in this game. There are many ways to play, from logistics to acting as close air support, to infantry. Many different play styles are supported through this game. Sure, if you want to try something new, you are definitely going to have to experience a leaning curve, but that's nothing compared to some mods for the game. The modding community for the game a very active, and there is something for everyone. From turning the game into straight up HALO, to smaller things for QOL like workable helmet lights or some prefabs for Editor or Zeus. Of course, some mods focus on realism to the max. Things like realistic starting procedures for F/A-18's or just mods for ambiance such as traffic and other things like that. Another thing to look at is the customization aspect in Arma. The virtual arsenal is a thing that you should first be introduced to in your first minutes on a Zeus multiplayer server, or your first few minutes trying to figure out hoe the Eden editor works. It allows complete customization of things from your weapons, clothes, and gear, all the way down to things like what you want in your gear when you start, like some extra ammo or a few grenades. You might want to watch out for the stamina system though. The more items you carry, the smaller the stamina bar gets. The stamina bar shows you how long you can sprint for, among other things. If you are loaded to the brim with items, you may be slowed to a walk, with no sprint bar. you would have to drop some of your items to get it back. Now here's the only reason that I don't like it. The DLCs are expensive and there are a lot of them. Sure, just don't get the DLC, but its not that simple. A lot of assets in Arma are locked by DLC content. Things from Jets and helicopters, all the way down to simple things such as clothes. It is possible to play Arma without said DLC content, but it is very locked down. If you really want to play Arma at its fullest, then you might want to purchase the DLCs. Other than that little bit, I love the game. It was a wonderful buy. If you are thinking of buying now thanks to my review, I would recommend waiting for a Christmas sale, or another sale. The game itself is worth a pretty penny, but I got it on sale for around thirty dollars. As a little heads-up, the game is set in 2035. That might sound like the content will be super futuristic, but it really isn't as futuristic as you would think. They put it in a semi-realistic perspective on how combat would be in the mid 2030s. Thats all for me, I hope that I shed some light on how the game is going to be for you. If it sounds like a good one, I hope that you would consider buying this game,  but if you don't, I won't hold it against you.
ARMA 3 provides a fun and semi-realistic. I have had tons of hours with my friends on here, and I can't wait to start it all again soon!
